_notes: What the presbyterate says (DESIGN §8.12). `kinds` are seeded by systems/talk.ts from what happened: about him (`you`) from his own record, about others from the watched men (the deanery, the pastor above him, his classmates, his confreres). Each kind has true versions and distortions; a rumour is true about `truth` of the time. `standing` is what the talk does to his standing with his brothers when it goes round (for talk about him), or a hint of its weight (about others). Templates use {name} (the subject as the talk names him), {parish}, {his}. Venues are where he hears it; `when` narrows some to a season. Numbers invented.

true: {name} has turned {parish} around; the numbers are real, the dean says.
{name} has {parish} coming back, and the men who had it before him have opinions about that.
false: {name} turned {parish} around by spending the school's endowment.
{name} is inflating the count at {parish}; the ushers write down what they are told.

true: {parish} is going under, and {name} is the man who has it.
{name} has lost the families at {parish}; they are at the parish on the hill.
false: {name} drove the families out of {parish} with a homily about the collection.
{name} has given up on {parish} and is looking at a chaplaincy.

true: {name} wrote that column, and the chancery read it twice.
{name} has been writing for the paper, and half the presbyterate agrees with him.
false: {name} wrote the column to get the bishop's attention, and got it.
{name} was told to write the column by someone at the chancery, which is why it said what it said.

true: {name} said in public what most of the men only say at dinner.
{name} took a stand, aloud, and the paper printed it.
false: {name} is running for something; nobody says that in public otherwise.
{name} said it to be on the record for the next bishop.

true: {name} was passed over, and took it well, or as well as anyone does.
{name} was on the terna and did not get it.
false: {name} was passed over because the bishop cannot stand him.
{name} was passed over after a letter from a parishioner, which the chancery has.

true: {name} is going up; the letter came from the chancery this month.
{name} has been named, and the men who were ahead of him have noticed.
false: {name} got it because someone in his family knows the bishop.
{name} asked for it, in writing, which is not done.

true: {name} looks worn out; the men who saw him at the deanery meeting said so.
{name} is running on nothing, and the parish has noticed before he has.
false: {name} is drinking, or that is what the tiredness is being called.
{name} has been seen at the doctor's twice, and nobody knows for what.

true: {name} has asked to be moved, which is on file now.
{name} wrote to the vicar for clergy about an assignment, and the vicar for clergy told the dean.
false: {name} asked for the cathedral, which is a thing you do not ask for.
{name} is going back to Rome, or to Washington, or somewhere with a degree in it.

true: {name} opened the hall to the shelter's men for the winter, and the finance council resigned over it.
{name} has twenty men sleeping in his hall, and the town knows which church was open.
false: {name} is running a shelter with no insurance and the chancery is furious.
{name} has the shelter's men in the church at night, and one of them took the candlesticks.

true: {name} sold the lot behind the hall, and cleared the parish's debt with it.
{name} sold the parish's lot to a developer, and the festival has nowhere to go.
false: {name} sold the lot to a friend of the mayor's for less than it was worth.
{name} sold the lot and the school's endowment is not where he said it would be.

true: {name} is drinking again; his vigil has been said by a retired man three Saturdays running.
{name} is drinking, and the dean has stopped pouring wine at the meeting.
false: {name} has been sent away; the parish was told a sabbatical.
{name} was found in his car in the parish lot on a Saturday night, or so the story goes.

true: {name} is worn out and not returning calls, and his secretary is covering for him.
{name} has stopped coming to the deanery meetings, and nobody has asked why.
false: {name} is leaving; he has told the bishop, or he is about to.
{name} has a breakdown coming, and the men are betting on the month.

true: {name} is thinking about leaving, and has told two people, which in this diocese is telling everyone.
{name} is looking at the door; you can see it in how he stands at the meetings.
false: {name} has a woman; there is always a woman in the story.
{name} has been offered a job by a university, which is how they always go.

true: {name} is ill, the kind with a schedule, and is keeping on as if it had none.
{name} is being treated in the city, and the dean is covering his Sundays.
false: {name} is dying, and the parish has not been told.
{name} has months; the vicar for clergy is already thinking about the parish.

true: {name}'s mother is dying in the next county, and he drives there on his days off.
{name} is looking after a parent, and it is taking the parish out of him.
false: {name} has moved his mother into the rectory, and the housekeeper has left.
{name} is never at the parish; the deacon runs it.

true: {name} has been moved, with a month's notice, to the far end of the diocese.
{name} is gone from the deanery; the letter came in the middle of the week.
false: {name} was moved because of something, and the chancery is not saying what.
{name} asked to be moved after a fight with the finance council that ended in the paper.

true: {name} has been made a pastor, which was overdue or was not, depending on who is telling it.
{name} has his own parish now, and the men who trained him say it about themselves.
false: {name} got the parish over two better men because he golfs with the vicar general.
{name} was made pastor to get him out of the last place before something came out.

true: {name} has gone to the chancery, which is a promotion or a sentence.
{name} is at the chancery now, and the men are careful what they say near him.
false: {name} went to the chancery because the bishop wants his own man near the files.
{name} asked for the chancery post, in writing, which the men do not forgive.

true: {name} is to be a bishop, elsewhere; the nuncio called on a Tuesday.
{name} has been named a bishop, and the class is dining out on it.
false: {name} was named because his uncle sat on a dicastery.
{name} campaigned for it, which nobody believes and everybody repeats.

true: {name} has left the priesthood; the letter to the men was two lines.
{name} is gone, and the parish was told a leave, and the men were told the truth.
false: {name} left with the parish's money, or with someone's wife, or both, depending on the telling.
{name} was pushed; the chancery has a file and the file has a page.

true: {name} has died. The funeral is at the cathedral, and the bishop will preach.
{name} died in the rectory, and the housekeeper found him, and the parish has not stopped talking.
false: {name} died of the drink, whatever the notice says.
{name} died alone, and nobody had visited in a year, which is said of every priest who dies.

true: {name} is in trouble, the kind that has lawyers in it, and the chancery has gone quiet.
{name} has been put on leave, and the men are saying less than they know.
false: {name} is in the paper next week; a reporter has been calling the deanery.
{name} has been moved to the monastery, which is what they do.

diocesan.label: The dean, in the parking lot after
At the confessors' dinner in Lent
In the cathedral sacristy before the Chrism Mass
At a funeral lunch, from a man you barely know

religious.label: A brother from another house, on the phone

aboutYouHeard: Someone let you know what is being said: {text}
{venue}, a man who meant well told you what they are saying: {text}
